terms.gloss: unsoundness of mind, madness; mad folly
evidence: Plaut. Amph. 798: jam tū quoque hujus adjuvās īnsāniam?
Cic. Tusc. 3.8: nōmen īnsāniae significat mentis aegrōtātiōnem et morbum (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: being out of one’s senses, madness
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 3.10: animī adfectiōnem lūmine mentis carentem nōmināvērunt āmentiam eandemque dēmentiam (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: being out of one’s mind; madness, folly
madness (properly of dogs); rage, fury, frenzy
evidence: Liv. 21.48.4: velut injectā rabiē ad arma itūrōs (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Ei mihi, jam tū quoque hujus adjuvās īnsāniam?
phrases.english: Oh dear, are you too now encouraging her in her madness?

phrases.latin: contāctōs eō scelere velut injectā rabiē ad arma itūrōs
phrases.english: that, tainted by that crime, they would rush to arms as if a madness had been cast on them

sources: Lewis & Short: insania · Lewis & Short: amentia · Lewis & Short: dementia
